items.title: Sci-fi RPG Exodus gets even more Mass Effect-like with its female lead, who they are calling Femjun
items.summary: Yup, it's official.
items.body: We've said previously that, for better or worse, the third-person sci-fi RPG Exodus looks a lot like Mass Effect. It's a characterization that developer Archetype Entertainment isn't shying away from—in fact, it seems to be actively embracing it with the reveal of the game's female protagonist, who they refer to as Femjun. I kid you not, this is not a name I've cooked up or run across on social media. It's right there on the Exodus website : "Meet Femjun! You’ve been waiting to see FemJun, and today we’re happy to say she’s finally here." Femjun is a very direct reference to Femshep, the female version of Commander Shepard in BioWare's Mass Effect trilogy. While the male version was effectively the default playable character through the first two games, BioWare took steps to put them on equal footing for Mass Effect 3. That effort included a vote to let fans decide the character's official face , which was subsequently used on alternate or inside covers of Mass Effect 3 packaging. Voiced by Jennifer Hale, Femshep became so popular that when BioWare dropped the Mass Effect Legendary Edition trailer, it was she who appeared most prominently . items.summary: The Game Awards says its judges "may be provided with advance or pre-release access to games for critical evaluation."
items.body: The Game Awards has announced its nominations slate for 2026, revealing that Grand Theft Auto 6 is this year's most-nominated game. Rockstar's hotly anticipated crime epic has secured eight nominations including Game of the Year, for which it'll be competing with games including Resident Evil Requiem, Control Resonant, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Now you—and the countless other people preparing to argue about this online—may have noticed that GTA 6 has been nominated for a number of awards despite the fact that it hasn't been released yet . In a press release, The Game Awards notes that jurors were in some cases provided with early access to enable awards consideration. "The nominees for The Game Awards are selected by a global jury of over 160 media publications and creator outlets around the world, who may be provided with advance or pre-release access to games for critical evaluation," The Game Awards said. items.title: Valve-sanctioned Half-Life remake Black Mesa gets a mondo update and a Steam Deck verified badge
items.summary: And cubemaps. Which, thank god.
items.body: Here's a terrifying reminder that the cold hand of Death is on my shoulder: I'm pretty sure I first played Black Mesa back in 2012, at the tender age of 19. In the intervening 14 years, the fan-made Half-Life 1 remake has walked quite the road, including getting Valve's official blessing to sell itself—for money!—on Steam in 2015. And they're still going, the mad lads. Just yesterday, Black Mesa got a hefty major update "featuring visual upgrades, engine optimizations, and a complete interface overhaul". It's called the Anomalous Improvements Update and it's a real humdinger. The biggest improvement—if you are me, a man who tries to play basically everything on his Steam Deck these days—is the Steam Deck verification and much-improved controller support. The game will now recognise and let you use a gamepad right from the jump, rather than forcing you to faff around in settings, and generally seems like a rather seamless delight on Deck in the little bit of time I've mucked about with it. items.title: Civilization dev Firaxis reportedly lays off a third of its staff, studio head departs
items.summary: A new XCOM game in development at Firaxis has reportedly struggled and missed a major milestone earlier this year.
items.body: A Bloomberg report says Civilization studio Firaxis has laid off roughly 60 people, representing about one-third of its total headcount. Heather Hazen, who took over as studio head in 2023 after more than 25 years with Firaxis, is also leaving. A 2K Games spokesperson didn't comment on the reported number of employees let go, but confirmed that layoffs had occurred in a statement provided to PC Gamer. "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years," the rep said. "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." The rep also confirmed that Hazen has stepped down as Firaxis studio head: "With the studio entering this reset, she feels this is the right, deliberate moment to hand over the reins to ensure the next studio leader has full ownership of this new era from the start." items.title: Jensen Huang says he would come back as Nvidia's CEO if America needs him – a technique I now intend to use at my next job interview
items.summary: "I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
items.body: Jensen Huang says he would be honoured to return to his role as Nvidia's CEO should the company's board want him. The problem for Huang is, the board don't seem to. In a statement sent to CNN , among others, Huang lays out his now clear-as-day faults and makes a pitch for his old job back. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang says. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." President Donald Trump and a cohort of silicon valley execs have previously backed the Nvidia co-founder, even if Trump did wobble his way over to backing ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook for a day. A heap of signatures were also added to a #bringjensenback petition , supposedly including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney. Sweeney has barely come up for air he's so wound up about Huang's resignation. items.body: Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, got in hot water late last month when he said, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time". He has since gone on to say he wants everyone to have RAM, actually, and in a conversation with Semafor , he has elaborated on what he claims he actually means (via The Verge ). Altman says, "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM. I think everybody should buy a lot of RAM, be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer. I think this is good. I think the home tinkering is great." So why the discrepancy? Altman says his comment was "misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it". items.title: AMD introduces Capacity Aware Scheduling to the Linux kernel, which sure is the thing I'd do if I were introducing Zen 6 LP cores next year
items.summary: Any way that more efficiently uses cores has the thumbs up from me.
items.body: AMD's Vishal Badole recently posted two Linux kernel patches (via TechPowerUp ), and these both pair up to introduce Capacity Aware Scheduling (CAS) for AMD heterogeneous processors. If that sounds like gibberish to you, effectively, this lays the groundwork to more efficiently handle AMD chips that have different core types. Up until now, AMD's performance scaling driver for Linux (amd-pstate) treated all cores as equal, assigning tasks regardless of core strength. AMD's current heterogeneous design pairs full-fat Zen 5 and lower-caste Zen 5C cores together in Zen 5 chips nowadays, but there is far less actual difference between these two core types than in the P-cores and E-cores of modern Intel architectures. But Zen 6's full lineup is currently suggested to be quite different. Also shared in a Linux patch earlier this year , Zen 6 is set to introduce a new Low Power core type (which is set to run at a very low power, as you might guess from the name), and that is a core type that would really benefit from Capacity Aware Scheduling. items.body: World of Warcraft: Forever has a unique problem—it's intended to be a "forever" version of baseline Azeroth, with no planned level-increasing expansions and an emphasis on horizontal progression with only minor vertical item level increases. But expansion packs are more than just a stack of a few levels, they're also an opportunity to adjust to the MMO economy. Which so often suffers because, well, you're essentially printing money all the time. Every enemy killed, every resource node farmed, every trash item sold, effectively adds more money into the world. There are ways to remove this money, sure. Repair costs, flight paths, goldsinks like a mount grind, dual spec, or respec fees. But if someone's dedicated to grinding, they can put together a hundred gold in a few hours. items.summary: There's always room for a bit more polish.
items.body: Working to a deadline is hard enough, but working towards one that can be moved if you really need it is worse. Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in the works for around a decade, including a couple of delays so devs could polish up some rough edges, and after all this time it must be really hard to step back and say enough is enough. "They would never stop working on this game if they had the choice," Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing, says in an interview with The Guardian . (Image credit: Rockstar) We now know that part of the reason why GTA 6 was delayed was because of the sheer amount of NPCs that needed kitting out with dialogue and audio. Talking to Bloomberg co-head of Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, explained how the delay wasn't strictly necessary but not delaying would have meant GTA 6 "won't be the game we want to make." Nelson expands on this with The Guardian: "It’s really hard to close it down. If you step away and get a little bit of space from it, you can look at it objectively and go: 'I'm proud of what we’ve done'.
